# Unused-objects baseline for the Artificial Intelligence Sample.
#
# Distilled from target/artificial-intelligence-unused-analysis.csv (an external
# unused-objects analysis export over the same model in samples/), one unique
# object per line — the export emits one row per consumer, deduplicated here:
#
#   <ripbi-type>\t<table>\t<object name>\t<expected chain>
#
# expected chain: "orphan"  — externally marked Unused (ripbi: empty used_by)
#                 "chained" — externally marked Used by unused (ripbi: every
#                             consumer itself unused)
#
# Objects the export marks dead that ripbi deliberately does NOT flag (they are
# asserted separately in tests/artificial_intelligence.rs, with reasons):
#   - nine columns kept alive only by bookmark saved filters — re-applying a
#     bookmark re-binds its fields, so ripbi counts bookmark state as usage and
#     the external analysis does not.
# Objects both sides mark dead, distilled out of the rows for their chain shape
# (asserted in the test): the two unactivated inactive SystemUserSeq
# relationships and their three key columns — externally Unused; ripbi flags
# the relationships themselves and chains the keys under them
# (`only used by … (also unused)`): nothing but a live USERELATIONSHIP
# reference can activate an inactive relationship, and the report has none.
# Objects ripbi flags that the export does not (asserted as the only extras):
#   - the engine-generated auto date/time machinery (LocalDateTable_* and
#     DateTableTemplate_* tables with their partitions), unused because the
#     report never references it except through the date variations this crate
#     deliberately does not model — a known gap, see docs/formats.md — plus the
#     four LocalDateTable hierarchy columns the export counts as used through
#     that machinery;
#   - the fully-dead 'Contacts' and 'Opportunity Forecast Adjustment' tables
#     with their partitions (the export lists no table rows; a table referenced
#     by nothing but a relationship is unused by the documented containment
#     rule);
#   - expression 'Query1', which the export does not track: nothing references
#     it except a leftover refresh-order annotation.
